# manual case: which branch of triage.py's invalid-probe classifier fires, per capture
#
# Not a dxc invocation. This re-derives, from the captures already on disk, the
# intermediate values inside scripts/triage.py's `classify()` so that the
# invalid-probe finding in method-notes.md can be re-checked without re-reading
# the classifier's control flow by eye.
#
# Read-only: it imports scripts/triage.py and calls matches(),
# _is_absence_predicate() and classify(). Nothing is written.
#
# Columns:
#   raw     -- what the predicate alone says: matches() -> repro | no-repro
#   absPred -- _is_absence_predicate(), i.e. can the "repro" branch demote?
#   marker  -- the substring of the output matched by classify()'s `unsupported`
#              regex, or "-" for none
#   final   -- classify()'s answer, which is what lands in the "# verdict:" header
#
# Branches in scripts/triage.py::classify() (line numbers at commit ab5400907):
#   A  line 688  verdict == "no-repro" and unsupported                  -> invalid-probe
#   B  line 703  verdict == "no-repro" and is_internal_failure(...)      -> invalid-probe
#   C  line 713  verdict == "repro" and _is_absence_predicate(...)
#                and (unsupported or is_internal_failure(...))           -> invalid-probe

# ran: 2026-08-07, from .github/skills/dxc-issue-triage
# cmd (PowerShell here-string piped to python -):
#
#   import sys, os, re
#   sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join("scripts"))
#   import triage as T
#   UNSUP = (r"(?i)invalid profile|unsupported profile|unrecognized (?:argument|option)|"
#            r"unknown argument|is not supported|requires shader model|"
#            r"CodeGen not available|recompile with -D|"
#            r"use of undeclared identifier|unknown type name|"
#            r"no member named|no matching function for call to|"
#            r"for non-scalar types use 'select'")
#   cases = [("out-main-debug.txt", "match.json"), ...]
#   d = T.issue_dir(3055)
#   for f, mf in cases:
#       meta, text = T.read_out(os.path.join(d, f))
#       rc = int(meta["exit"]) & 0xFFFFFFFF
#       raw  = "repro" if T.matches(3055, text, rc, False, mf) else "no-repro"
#       absp = T._is_absence_predicate(3055, mf)
#       m    = re.search(UNSUP, text)
#       fin  = T.classify(3055, text, rc, False, mf)
#       print(f, raw, absp, m.group(0) if m else "-", fin)

capture                                                        raw       absPred  marker                           final
out-main-debug.txt                                             repro     True     -                                repro
variant-gatherred-main-debug--match-gatherred.txt              repro     True     -                                repro
variant-methodology-freefn-main-debug--match-methodology-freefn.txt no-repro  True     no matching function for call to invalid-probe
variant-methodology-arity-main-debug--match-methodology-arity.txt repro     True     use of undeclared identifier     invalid-probe
variant-control-arity-main-debug.txt                           no-repro  True     -                                no-repro
variant-control-correct-sampler-main-debug.txt                  no-repro  True     -                                no-repro

# Reading of the table:
#
# Rows 1-2 and 5-6 are #3055's own probes and controls. None of their output
# carries a marker, so `final` == `raw` throughout and the classifier is inert
# for this issue. That is the negative result: #3055's verdict is not affected.
#
# Row 3 is branch A. dxc compiled the shader, ran overload resolution, and
# emitted a COMPLETE and CORRECT diagnostic naming the failed conversion. For a
# diagnostic-quality issue that is precisely what a FIX looks like, and it is
# recorded as "this compiler never ran the repro".
#
# Row 4 is branch C. dxc emitted the reported symptom -- the predicate matched --
# and the probe is still discarded, because the symptom text IS a marker.
#
# The dependence is on one word. Row 1's message is "no matching MEMBER function
# for call to"; the marker is "no matching function for call to". Delete the word
# "member" -- which is what dxc prints for a free intrinsic, row 3 -- and #3055's
# own ground-truth probe becomes invalid-probe.
